subject: General Knowledge
description: GI Act 1999, India's first GI, state-product matching, recent additions

questions.stem: Geographical Indication (GI) tags in India are governed by which Act?

options.option_text: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999

questions.explanation: The GI Act, 1999 — came into force 15 September 2003. Administered by the Geographical Indications Registry, Chennai, under the Office of the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM). India is a signatory to TRIPS (1995) which mandates GI protection. A GI is granted for goods (including agricultural, natural, manufactured) tied to a specific geographical origin and possessing qualities/reputation due to that origin.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the FIRST product in India to receive a GI tag?
questions.explanation: Darjeeling Tea — registered as India's first GI in 2004. The Tea Board of India holds the GI. Darjeeling tea is grown in 87 specific tea gardens of the Darjeeling district, West Bengal, at altitudes between 600-2,000 m. The next firsts were Aranmula Kannadi (Kerala metal mirror) and Pochampally Ikat (Telangana). India had ~600+ GIs by early 2026 — Karnataka and Tamil Nadu lead the state-wise tally.

questions.stem: 'Naga Mircha' (King Chilli / Bhut Jolokia) — once the world's hottest chilli — has a GI tag from which state?
questions.explanation: Naga Mircha — Bhut Jolokia / Ghost Pepper / King Chilli — was certified the world's hottest in 2007 (Guinness, ~10,00,000 SHU). GI granted to Nagaland in 2008. Same chilli is also grown in Assam and Manipur but the GI is held by Nagaland. India also has GIs for several spices: Khola Chilli (Goa), Byadagi Chilli (Karnataka), Kashmir Saffron, Coorg Green Cardamom, Malabar Pepper, Alleppey Green Cardamom.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the GI-tagged product with its state — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Kanjeevaram (Kanchipuram) Silk is from Tamil Nadu, NOT Kerala. Kerala's iconic GIs include Aranmula Kannadi (metal mirror), Wayanad Robusta Coffee, Marayoor Jaggery, Nilambur Teak, Edayur Chilli, Palakkadan Matta Rice. The other three options are correct: Pashmina (J&K), Tirupati Laddu (AP, 2009 — first food product GI), Mysore Sandal Soap (Karnataka, KSDL, has been made since 1916).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: A GI tag is granted for an initial period of:

options.option_text: 10 years (renewable for further periods of 10 years)

questions.explanation: Section 18 of GI Act, 1999 — initial registration is for 10 years from the date of filing. Can be renewed indefinitely for further 10-year periods on payment of renewal fee. Compare: Patent — 20 years (one-time, no renewal); Trademark — 10 years renewable; Copyright — author's lifetime + 60 years; Design — 10 years + 5 year extension. GI rights are held by an association of producers / regulator, not a single owner.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Madhubani painting — known for its distinctive geometric patterns and bright colours — received a GI tag for which state?
questions.explanation: Madhubani (also called Mithila) painting — from the Madhubani district of Bihar (Mithila region). GI granted in 2007. Originally created by women on freshly plastered mud walls of huts; now also done on cloth, paper, canvas. Themes — Hindu deities, royal court scenes, social events. Famous artists — Sita Devi, Ganga Devi, Bharti Dayal. Other Bihar GIs include Bhagalpur Silk, Mithila Makhana (2022), Katarni Rice.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which state has the highest number of GI tags in India (as of early 2026)?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu leads the state-wise GI tally with 60+ registrations as of early 2026, ahead of Karnataka (~50), Uttar Pradesh, Kerala and Maharashtra. TN's diverse GIs include Kanchipuram Silk, Madurai Sungudi, Salem Silk, Ooty Tea, Eathomozhy Tall Coconut, Thanjavur Veenai, Madurai Malli (jasmine), Toda embroidery, Coimbatore Wet Grinders, and the iconic Tirunelveli Halwa. Tamil Nadu's strong handicraft + agricultural traditions make it a natural leader.
